name: rtw89_ops_change_vif_links
prose: mac80211 change_vif_links callback (mac80211.c:1645). Asserts the wiphy lock. Returns -EOPNOTSUPP, before any change, if rtw89_can_work_on_links(rtwdev, vif, new_links) is false. When links are being removed (old_links == 0 or some link is cleared) it kzallocs a snapshot of the old bss_conf pointers (-ENOMEM on failure, nothing else done yet) and publishes it in rtwvif->snap_link_confs. It then leaves IPS (rtw89_leave_ips_by_hwflags), aborts a running scan, and calls rtw89_vif_update_fw_links(rtwdev, rtwvif, old_links, true); then clears the idle link if old_links was 0, else clears clr_links if non-empty. If it removed links it resets snap_link_confs to NULL, calls synchronize_rcu and kfrees the snapshot. Then if set_links is non-empty it sets those links (on failure it clears them again) and keeps the error in ret; else if new_links is 0 it sets the idle link (clearing it on failure). If ret is 0 it calls rtw89_vif_update_fw_links(rtwdev, rtwvif, new_links, false). It then re-enters IPS (rtw89_enter_ips_by_hwflags) and returns ret (0 or the set-links error). The effect of the two update_fw_links calls (what is sent to firmware, and whether the ml_trans state set elsewhere is needed) was not read, so no claim about firmware updates is made.
note: Reviewers: original and round 15 both concern rtw89_vif_update_fw_links internals (not read); the visible code of this function is described above. The -ENOMEM and -EOPNOTSUPP early returns come before the IPS leave, so enter_ips is not called on those paths.

name: get_mcs_ra_mask
prose: Pure static helper (phy.c:53) that builds a rate-adaptation bitmask from a 2-bit-per-stream MCS map. It loops i = 0..3 over the 4 two-bit fields of mcs_map (low field first), with nss starting at 12 and increasing by 12 per field (shift 12, 24, 36, 48). For field value 2 it ORs GENMASK_ULL(highest_mcs, 0) << nss; for 1 it ORs GENMASK_ULL(highest_mcs - gap, 0) << nss; for 0 it ORs GENMASK_ULL(highest_mcs - gap*2, 0) << nss; for 3 (and nothing else) it adds nothing. It returns the accumulated u64. It has no side effects, takes no locks and touches no global state. GENMASK_ULL with a high bit below 0 (when highest_mcs < gap or highest_mcs < 2*gap in the respective case) is not valid, so callers must pass highest_mcs >= 2*gap.
note: Reviewer round 15 (contract omits no-side-effect statement) is moot: contract is left empty because the old formal contract used int shifts of up to 48 bits and did not parse/verify in earlier rounds. Prose verified against phy.c:59-76.

name: rtw89_phy_txpwr_dbm_to_mac
prose: Static inline (phy.h:977) converting a dBm value to the MAC tx-power unit. It computes dbm << rtwdev->chip->txpwr_factor_mac in int (dbm is s8, promoted; shifting a negative dbm left is not well-defined C), converts that int to s16 in clamp_t(s16, ..., -64, 63), so a result outside the s16 range would first wrap, then clamps it to the range -64..63, and returns that as s8. The clamp range includes negative values (-64..-1), so the result is not limited to 0..63. It reads only rtwdev->chip->txpwr_factor_mac; it has no side effects.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (negative dbm left shift), round 2/15 right (clamp is to [-64,63], s16 truncation before clamp, phy.h:981). Contract left empty (reads chip state, shifts a possibly negative value).

name: _dpk_pas_read
prose: Static DPK helper (rtw8851b_rfk.c:2289, returns u8). It does return a value: the final comparison at 2327-2332. It writes the PAS-read configuration registers (R_KIP_RPT1, R_DPK_CFG2, R_DPK_CFG3). If is_check is non-zero it reads two (I,Q) pairs from R_RPT_COM at index 0 and index 0x1f, takes the absolute value of the 12-bit sign-extended I and Q parts, and logs the ratio PAS_delta; if is_check is 0 it only loops over 32 indexes writing R_DPK_CFG3 and logging each report word, and leaves all four value variables at 0. In both cases it then computes sqrt-sum values val1 = I1^2 + Q1^2 and val2 = I2^2 + Q2^2 (both 0 when is_check is 0) and returns 2 if val1 < val2, else 1 if val1 >= val2 * 8 / 5, else 0. So with is_check == 0 it returns 1 (0 >= 0), and with is_check != 0 it returns 2, 1 or 0 by that comparison.
note: Reviewers: rounds 1 and 2 WRONG (the function has returns at rtw8851b_rfk.c:2328-2332); round 15 right (is_check=0 gives 1). Callee register helpers not read.

name: _iqk_one_shot
prose: Runs one IQK calibration step on an RTL8852A path (rtw8852a_rfk.c:802, static bool). It picks addr_rfc_ctl = 0x5864 for path A else 0x7864 and always sends the BTC notification BTC_WRFK_ONESHOT_START first (817), before the ktype switch. Per ktype it builds iqk_cmd: ID_TXAGC and ID_RXAGC only build the command (no register writes before the shot); ID_FLOK_COARSE, ID_FLOK_FINE, ID_RXK and ID_NBRXK set bit 0x20000000 of addr_rfc_ctl and write R_IQK_DIF4 (TXT 0x009 for the FLOK types, RXT 0x011 for the RX types); ID_TXK and ID_NBTXK clear that bit and write R_IQK_DIF4 TXT 0x025. For an unknown ktype it returns false right away, after the START notification but without sending STOP, writing the command or clearing addr_rfc_ctl (857-858). For the known types it writes iqk_cmd + 1 to R_NCTL_CFG, sets R_DPK_CTL enable, delays 1 us, takes fail from _iqk_check_cal, optionally reads XYM, FFT, SRAM and (TX CFIR for ID_TXK, RX CFIR for every other ktype) data depending on the iqk_info enable flags, clears bit 0x20000000 of addr_rfc_ctl, sends BTC_WRFK_ONESHOT_STOP and returns fail.
note: Reviewers: original right (unknown ktype sends START then returns false, no STOP); round 15 right (ID_TXAGC and ID_RXAGC do not program R_IQK_DIF4/RFC bits, 819-821 and 838-840). Callee bodies not read.

name: _dpk_lbk_rxiqk
prose: Runs the DPK loopback RX IQ calibration for one path (rtw8852b_rfk.c:1832, static void, no return value). It reads the current RX baseband gain (RR_MOD RXBB field) and then: enables MDPK_RX_DCK, zeroes the RXCFIR result field of R_IQK_RES for the path, copies RR_CFGCH into RR_RSV4, sets RR_MOD mode to 0xd, sets RR_RXK PLLEN, sets RR_TXIQK ATT1 to 0x13 if the RXBB value is >= 0x11, 0x00 if it is <= 0x0a, else 0x05, clears RR_XGLNA2 SW and RR_RXKPLL POW, writes 0x80014 to RR_RXKPLL, waits 70 us, sets R_P0_RFCTM_EN and R_IQK_DIF4 RXT = 0x025, runs _dpk_one_shot(LBK_RXIQK), and logs R_RXIQC. Afterwards it clears R_P0_RFCTM_EN (so that bit is restored to 0), clears RR_RXK PLLEN, clears MDPK_RX_DCK_EN and R_KPATH_CFG_ED, sets R_LOAD_COEF DI to 1 and sets RR_MOD mode to 0x5. It does not restore the earlier values of RR_RSV4, RR_TXIQK ATT1, RR_XGLNA2 SW, RR_RXKPLL, R_IQK_DIF4 RXT or the R_IQK_RES RXCFIR field; these keep the values written above. Callee _dpk_one_shot not read.
note: Reviewers: original right (RSV4, TXIQK ATT1, RXKPLL, DIF4 are not restored); round 15 right (R_P0_RFCTM_EN is cleared at 1868, and RR_XGLNA2 SW is changed at 1855).

name: _iqk_one_shot
prose: Runs one IQK step on an RTL8852B path (rtw8852b_rfk.c:815, static bool). For an unknown ktype it returns false immediately (858-859), before writing anything and before clearing B_P0_RFCTM_EN. For known ktypes it builds iqk_cmd: FLOK_COARSE, FLOK_FINE, FLOK_VBUFFER, RXK and NBRXK set B_P0_RFCTM_EN to 1 first; TXK and NBTXK set it to 0 first; RXAGC writes no R_P0_RFCTM_EN value before the shot; NBTXK writes R_IQK_DIF4 TXT 0x011 and NBRXK writes R_IQK_DIF4 RXT 0x011. It then writes iqk_cmd + 1 to R_NCTL_CFG, waits 1 us, sets fail = _iqk_check_cal(rtwdev, path), writes B_P0_RFCTM_EN = 0 and returns fail. So B_P0_RFCTM_EN is cleared after every known-ktype shot (including RXAGC) but not on the unknown-ktype return.
note: Reviewers: original right (unknown ktype returns before clearing RFCTM_EN); round 15 right (ID_RXAGC does not write RFCTM_EN before the shot, 840-842). _iqk_check_cal not read.

name: rtw89_tas_track
prose: Static bool (sar.c:778) running one TAS (transmit antenna selection power) tracking step. In order: returns false if the TAS dynamic mechanism bit is set in hal->disabled_dm_bitmap; returns false if rtw89_tas_is_active() is false; if rtw89_tas_query_sar_config fails OR tas->block_regd is set it returns the result of __rtw89_tas_state_update(rtwdev, RTW89_TAS_STATE_STATIC_SAR) (so not necessarily false, and the state update happens before the pause check); then returns false if tas->pause is set (this check comes after the query and the block_regd test); otherwise it calls rtw89_tas_window_update and rtw89_tas_history_update and returns rtw89_tas_rolling_average(rtwdev). The meaning of the returned bool beyond these callee results was not read.
note: Reviewers: original right and round 15 right (paused is tested after query/block, sar.c:790-794). Callees not read.

name: blake2b_update
prose: Feeds inlen bytes from in into an initialised blake2b_state (blake2b.c:358). It has one return statement, return 0 at line 385, so it returns 0 for every input including inlen == 0 (no pointer or finalised-state check is made). While inlen > 0 it computes left = S->buflen and fill = 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES - left. If inlen > fill it copies fill bytes into S->buf, adds the block counter for one block, compresses the first block of the buffer, moves the second block down to the first, subtracts BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES from buflen and advances in/inlen by fill. Otherwise (inlen <= fill) it copies the remaining inlen bytes into the buffer after left, increases buflen by inlen and ends. Because compression only happens when input exceeds the space left, after the call S->buflen can equal 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES (when the buffer is exactly full), i.e. up to two whole blocks stay buffered and uncompressed; it is never above that. The caller must have initialised S so that buflen <= 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES and S->buf has space for 2 blocks.
note: Reviewers: original right (buflen can equal 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES, line 376-379); round 15 right (full blocks stay buffered; compression only when inlen > fill, line 365).

name: sc25519_reduce
prose: Reduces a 64-byte little-endian scalar modulo the Ed25519 group order l = 2^252 + 27742317777372353535851937790883648493 in place (ed25519_ref10.c:1557, void; the name sc_reduce in the packet is not the real name). It reads s[0..63] (through load_3/load_4 into 24 21-bit limbs s0..s23), performs the fixed sequence of limb multiplications, carries and subtractions of the reference ref10 reduction without any branch or return, and finally stores exactly 32 bytes s[0] .. s[31] (32 byte stores, none to s[32] or higher). On return the first 32 bytes hold the little-endian value of the input mod l; bytes s[32]..s[63] are not written by this function and keep their input values. The caller must supply a writable 64-byte buffer. No allocation, no locks.
note: Slice cut the head (function begins at ed25519_ref10.c:1557, ends 1878, under sys/contrib/libsodium/src/libsodium/). Arithmetic correctness of the limb reduction was not re-derived; I checked the loads (reads up to s+58..63 range via load_3(s+55)... shown at 1562-1590 in part) and the 32 final stores only (partly read: limb arithmetic lines 1585-1830 not checked line by line).

name: crypto_generichash_blake2b_final
prose: Thin wrapper (generichash_blake2b.c:100) that does assert(outlen <= UINT8_MAX) (a no-op when NDEBUG is defined) and returns blake2b_final(state, out, (uint8_t) outlen), so outlen is truncated to 8 bits if the assert is compiled out. The callee (blake2b-ref.c:290) calls sodium_misuse() (which does not return) if the 8-bit outlen is 0 or greater than BLAKE2B_OUTBYTES (64); it returns -1 without writing anything if the state is already finalised (blake2b_is_lastblock); otherwise it compresses any extra full block, pads and compresses the last block, writes the first outlen bytes of the 64-byte state hash into out (it does not compare outlen with the digest length stored in the state at init time), zeroes S->h and S->buf with sodium_memzero and returns 0. So the result is 0 or -1, and a state that returned 0 is wiped and must not be reused.
note: Reviewers: original right (the state must be initialised and not finalised, else -1); round 2 right (the output length is the caller's outlen, not the state's, blake2b-ref.c:323); round 15 right (nothing enforces outlen >= state outlen; the only checks are 0 < outlen <= 64 and the finalised-state check).

name: GetMacAddrHashCode
prose: Pure static function (memac.c:57) that computes a 6-bit multicast hash from the low 48 bits of ethAddr (a local copy, shifted away; the argument is by value). For i = 0..5 it XORs the 8 bits 8*i .. 8*i+7 of the original value (mask1 takes bit 8i, then XOR with the next 7 bits) and ORs that parity bit into bit (5 - i) of the result. Bits 48..63 of the input are never read. The result is therefore in 0..63 and bit 5 is the parity of the first (lowest) byte and bit 0 the parity of the sixth byte. No side effects, no locks, no allocation.
note: Earlier contract attempts (round 1 random test failure, rounds 0/15 syntax) are replaced by a simple bound that follows from the loop: only bits 0..5 of xorVal are ever set (memac.c:75). Prose from the old text agreed with the code.

name: MatchTableSet
prose: Static t_Error (fm_cc.c:4324-4903) that fills in a CC (coarse classification) match-table node p_CcNode from p_CcNodeParam. The slice began in the middle (statistics-mode fix-up at 4363). The function asserts its three arguments non-NULL (ASSERT_COND), mallocs p_GlblMask (CC_GLBL_MASK_SIZE bytes) and memsets it without checking for NULL (4350-4352), copies key counts, mask support and statistics mode into the node, and, if maxNumOfKeys is 0 and the statistics mode is NONE, forces the mode to FRAME (4363-4365). It then obtains the MURAM handle, initialises the lists and a spinlock, and decodes the extraction parameters (by header, non-header, IC etc.) into parseCode, offsets and sizes. From that point every failure first calls DeleteNode(p_CcNode) (or FM_PCD_MatchTableDelete later) and then returns an error: E_INVALID_HANDLE if no MURAM handle (4368-4369, before any DeleteNode), E_NO_MEMORY if the spinlock cannot be created, E_INVALID_STATE / E_INVALID_SELECTION / E_INVALID_VALUE for inconsistent or unsupported extraction parameters (e.g. unknown extraction type, illegal parse code, sizeOfExtraction above FM_PCD_MAX_SIZE_OF_KEY, keySize != sizeOfExtraction, hash-indexed offset+size > 8), the error of CheckParams/IcHashIndexedCheckParams, CalcAndUpdateCcShadow or AllocStatsObjs, and E_NO_MEMORY when MURAM allocation of the temporary AD, key match table or AD table fails. It copies each key (and local mask) into the key table and writes each next-engine AD (with stats objects when statisticsEn is set), handles the miss entry, takes FmPcdLockTryLockAll: if that fails it deletes the table and returns E_BUSY; then applies required actions for each next engine (on failure unlocks, deletes the table and returns the error), unlocks and returns E_OK. So on any error return after the early part the node has already been torn down by this function; on success the caller owns the populated node (it does not return a handle; the node pointer is an argument).
note: Real function found; the earlier drop was only because the head was cut. Partly read: lines 4383-4560 (extraction-type switch, I only checked the error returns and the DeleteNode calls) and 4640-4720, 4789-4855 (miss-entry and manipulation bookkeeping) were not read in detail. The unchecked XX_Malloc at 4350 is real.

name: FmPcdCcTreeAddIPR
prose: Adds IP-reassembly (IPR) groups to a CC tree (fm_cc.c:5046). Asserts the tree pointer non-NULL. It asks whether the reassembly manip carries an IPv6 header (FmPcdManipIpReassmIsIpv6Hdr). It returns E_INVALID_VALUE if IPv6 is present and tree->numOfEntries > FM_PCD_MAX_NUM_OF_CC_GROUPS - 2, or (for any case) if numOfEntries > FM_PCD_MAX_NUM_OF_CC_GROUPS - 1; so the tree may hold at most MAX-2 entries with IPv6 and at most MAX-1 without. It then tries the root lock (CcRootTryLock); on failure it returns E_BUSY. With the lock held: if tree->h_IpReassemblyManip already equals the given manip it releases the lock and returns E_OK without adding any group or entry (nothing consumed); if a different manip is already set it releases the lock and returns E_INVALID_STATE. Otherwise, for IPv6 it takes the next group id (numOfGrps++), sets that group's base entry to MAX-2, optionally builds the reassembly scheme (createSchemes; on failure it decrements numOfGrps, releases the lock and returns the error) and writes a DONE next-engine AD at entry MAX-2; then for IPv4 it takes the next group id, sets totalBitsMask 0 and base entry MAX-1, optionally builds the IPv4 scheme (on failure it decrements numOfGrps, also again for IPv6 when present with FmPcdManipDeleteIpReassmSchemes, releases the lock and returns the error), writes the DONE AD at entry MAX-1, stores the manip in the tree, releases the lock and returns E_OK.
note: Reviewers: original right (E_OK without consuming entries if the same IPR is already set, 5084-5088); round 15 right (the checks require at least one free entry (two with IPv6): fm_cc.c:5069-5074 test numOfEntries > MAX-2 / MAX-1). Callees not read.

name: BuildSchemeRegs
prose: Static t_Error (fm_kg.c:1009-1834; the slice 1107-1378 is a middle part) that fills a struct fman_kg_scheme_regs and the software scheme state from a KG scheme parameter block. It memsets the register block to zero, then returns E_INVALID_VALUE if numOfDistinctionUnits exceeds FM_PCD_MAX_NUM_OF_DISTINCTION_UNITS; for a non-alwaysDirect scheme it gets the netEnv id and the matching vector (E_INVALID_STATE if PcdGetUnitsVector fails), else it sets matchVector to SCHEME_ALWAYS_DIRECT and netEnvId to ILLEGAL_NETENV. It returns E_INVALID_STATE if nextEngine is e_FM_PCD_INVALID; E_NOT_SUPPORTED for bypassFqidGeneration on unsupported FM revisions, and E_INVALID_VALUE if bypassFqidGeneration is set with a non-zero baseFqid. For the PLCR next engine it records direct/absolute and returns E_INVALID_STATE for indirect policing with a shared profile; for the CC next engine it queries the tree group (FmPcdCcGetGrpParams, error passed on) and returns E_INVALID_VALUE (not E_INVALID_STATE) when a shared profile is requested in a KG->CC->PLCR flow (fm_kg.c:1219; a different shared-profile check at 1119 does return E_INVALID_STATE). Further E_INVALID_VALUE returns cover fqidOffsetShift too large and numOfProfiles zero or not a power of two, hash and extract parameters out of range, etc.; E_NOT_SUPPORTED, E_FULL (generic registers exhausted), E_INVALID_SELECTION and E_NO_MEMORY returns appear in the extract section. At the end it checks baseFqid fits in 24 bits (E_INVALID_VALUE), sets kgse_fqb, records nextEngine and doneAction in p_Scheme and returns E_OK. Many of the intermediate scheme fields (matchVector, netEnvId, ccUnits, directPlcr, etc.) are therefore already written into p_Scheme when a later error is returned.
note: Slice cut the head. Partly read: the register-composition sections 1177-1300 and the generic extract loops 1380-1800 (I only collected the RETURN_ERROR codes there, not the register values). Reviewer round 17 right: KG->CC->PLCR shared-profile misuse returns E_INVALID_VALUE at fm_kg.c:1219 (prose said E_INVALID_STATE for that case).

name: CheckManipParamsAndSetType
prose: Static t_Error (fm_manip.c:2527-2655) that validates a header-manipulation request and sets p_Manip->opcode (and sometimes muramAllocate). Exactly one branch is taken: remove, else insert, else frag/reassembly. Remove (u.hdr.rmv) is accepted only for rmvParams type BY_HDR / FROM_START: with include set and header CAPWAP_DTLS it sets opcode CAPWAP_RMV_DTLS_IF_EXIST and muramAllocate = TRUE, returns E_INVALID_STATE if insrt is also set, and, if fragOrReasm is set, accepts only non-frag reassembly with header CAPWAP (opcode becomes CAPWAP_REASSEMBLY) and returns E_INVALID_STATE otherwise (frag, or another header); with include clear and header CAPWAP_DTLS or CAPWAP it returns E_INVALID_STATE if fragOrReasm or insrt is set, else sets opcode HMAN_OC_RMV_N_OR_INSRT_INT_FRM_HDR, muramAllocate = TRUE and WRITES p_ManipParams->u.hdr.insrt = TRUE (it modifies the caller's parameter block). Any other remove type, location or header returns E_INVALID_STATE. Insert (only when rmv is not set) supports only the by-template type: opcode INSRT_HDR_BY_TEMPL_N_OR_FRAG_AFTER with muramAllocate = FALSE, changed to CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION when fragOrReasm with frag and CAPWAP header is requested; other fragOrReasm combinations and insert types return E_INVALID_STATE. Frag/reassembly alone: frag with CAPWAP sets opcode CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION and muramAllocate FALSE; reassembly alone always returns E_INVALID_STATE. If none of rmv, insrt, fragOrReasm is set it returns E_INVALID_STATE. Because opcode/muramAllocate are assigned before some of the later E_INVALID_STATE returns, a failing call can leave those fields modified in p_Manip. On success it copies insrt and rmv from the params into p_Manip->insrt and p_Manip->rmv (2651-2652) and returns E_OK.
note: Reviewers: original right (opcode/muramAllocate can be set before an E_INVALID_STATE return, e.g. 2542-2545); round 15 WRONG: the function does copy insrt and rmv into p_Manip at fm_manip.c:2651-2652.

name: FmPcdManipInitUpdate
prose: Static t_Error dispatcher (fm_manip.c:4562-4621) that initialises or updates the AD for a manipulation according to p_Manip->opcode. It first applies SANITY_CHECK_RETURN_ERROR(h_Manip, E_INVALID_HANDLE) (macro: returns the handle error when h_Manip is NULL). The level and h_FmTree arguments are marked UNUSED in this function body (they are passed to a callee only in the FM_CAPWAP_SUPPORT / DPAA_VERSION == 10 block), so no valid tree handle is required by this function itself. By opcode: HMAN_OC_IP_REASSEMBLY calls UpdateInitReasm; HMAN_OC_IP_FRAGMENTATION calls UpdateInitIpFrag; with DPAA_VERSION >= 11, HMAN_OC_CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION calls UpdateInitCapwapFrag and HMAN_OC_CAPWAP_REASSEMBLY calls UpdateInitReasm; in a DPAA 1.0 CAPWAP build additional cases exist (MV_INT_FRAME_HDR..., INSRT_HDR_BY_TEMPL with a frag handle, CAPWAP_RMV_DTLS_IF_EXIST with h_Frag, CAPWAP_INDEXED_STATS); for the INSRT_HDR_BY_TEMPL case with h_Frag NULL and for CAPWAP_RMV_DTLS_IF_EXIST with h_Frag NULL the function does no callee call and returns E_OK. Any other opcode returns E_OK at once with no effect. Otherwise it returns the callee's error code (E_OK on success). It takes no locks of its own here; callee behaviour was not read.
note: Reviewers: original right (E_OK no-op returns for known opcodes when h_Frag is NULL, 4584-4593, build-dependent); round 15 right (h_FmTree is UNUSED at 4573; it is only referenced inside the capwap-DPAA1 block).

name: FM_PCD_ManipNodeSet
prose: Public function returning a t_Handle (fm_manip.c:5198-5342; the packet name FM_PCD_ManipNodeCreate is not in this file, the slice cut the head). It applies SANITY_CHECK_RETURN_VALUE on h_FmPcd and p_ManipParams (NULL return with E_INVALID_HANDLE if either is NULL) and calls ManipOrStatsSetNode(h_FmPcd, params, FALSE); a NULL result is returned as NULL. For opcodes HMAN_OC_IP_REASSEMBLY, IP_FRAGMENTATION, HMAN_OC, IPSEC_MANIP (and, for DPAA_VERSION >= 11, CAPWAP_MANIP, CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION, CAPWAP_REASSEMBLY) it requires FmPcdIsAdvancedOffloadSupported; if not, it reports E_INVALID_STATE, frees p_Manip with XX_Free and returns NULL. It then creates a spinlock (XX_InitSpinlock); on failure it reports an error, calls ReleaseManipHandler, frees p_Manip and returns NULL. It initialises the node list and switches on p_Manip->opcode to the matching setup routine: IpReassembly, IpFragmentation followed by IPManip (stopping at the first error), IPSecManip, CapwapReassembly, CapwapFragmentation, CapwapManip (DPAA >= 11), or CreateManipActionNew for HMAN_OC; extra cases exist under FM_CAPWAP_SUPPORT with DPAA_VERSION == 10; an unknown opcode reports E_INVALID_VALUE, releases the handler, frees p_Manip and returns NULL. If the selected routine returns an error it reports it, calls ReleaseManipHandler, frees p_Manip and returns NULL. On success, if p_ManipParams->h_NextManip is set it stores it in p_Manip->h_NextManip, sets the next manip's previous pointer to p_Manip and increments its owner count (FmPcdManipUpdateOwner(..., TRUE)); it returns p_Manip, owned by the caller. On the failure paths this function does not free the spinlock itself (any release is inside ReleaseManipHandler, not read).
note: Real function is FM_PCD_ManipNodeSet; slice cut the head. Partly read: ManipOrStatsSetNode, the per-opcode setup routines and ReleaseManipHandler bodies were not read, so what they allocate and release is not claimed.

name: BuildProfileRegs
prose: Static t_Error (fm_plcr.c:334-530) that builds the policer profile register image in p_PlcrRegs. It asserts p_FmPcd. It returns E_NOT_AVAILABLE if FmGetTimeStampScale returns 0, and returns the error of SetProfileNia if converting the green, yellow or red next-engine parameters fails (those three NIA values are then stored at the end). pemode starts at FM_PCD_PLCR_PEMODE_PI. Pass-through: sets pecir, pecbs, pepepir_eir, pepbs_ebs, pelts, pects and pepts_ets all to 0 (token buckets are NOT set full), clears the algorithm bits, and for colour-blind mode sets the blind bit and the default colour (E_INVALID_SELECTION for an unknown default colour), for colour-aware clears it; any other colour mode returns E_INVALID_SELECTION. RFC 2698: returns E_INVALID_SELECTION if committedInfoRate > peakOrExcessInformationRate; RFC 2698 and RFC 4115 share the continuation: colour-blind sets the blind bit, colour-aware clears it and selects the override colour (E_INVALID_SELECTION for an invalid value), then the rate mode: byte mode selects frame-length and roll-back selections (E_INVALID_SELECTION for invalid values), packet mode sets the PKT bit, other modes are E_INVALID_SELECTION; then CalcRates fills cir, cbs, pir_eir, pbs_ebs and the floating-point position into the registers, and pepts_ets and pects are set to 0xFFFFFFFF (full buckets) here. Any other algSelection returns E_INVALID_SELECTION. On success it stores pemode and the three NIAs and zeroes the five colour counters pegpc, peypc, perpc, perypc and perrpc (fm_plcr.c:523-527), then returns E_OK. Registers assigned before a later error return stay partly written in p_PlcrRegs.
note: Reviewers: original right (pass-through sets buckets to 0, 364-370); round 15 WRONG: the five colour counters are zeroed at fm_plcr.c:523-527. Callee SetProfileNia and CalcRates not read.

name: SetPcd
prose: Static t_Error (fm_port.c:1111-1668) that programs a port's PCD (parser/keygen/CC/policer) configuration. Early checks, each returning an error before any register write: SANITY_CHECK E_INVALID_STATE if p_FmPortDriverParam is still set (port not yet initialised), E_INVALID_OPERATION for independent-mode ports and for port types other than RX, RX_10G and offline-parsing, E_INVALID_STATE for pcdSupport NONE or an unknown value, E_INVALID_VALUE if the parser's numOfHdrsWithAdditionalParams exceeds FM_PCD_PRS_NUM_OF_HDRS, and E_INVALID_STATE when the presence of the PRS, KG and CC parameter blocks does not match pcdSupport (the PLCR parameter block is not part of that consistency check). It sets p_FmPort->netEnvId and pcdEngines (written before these later checks fail). With CC it binds the tree (FmPcdCcBindTree, error returned) and writes the CC base register. With KG it requires at least one scheme (E_INVALID_VALUE), calls FmPcdKgSetOrBindToClsPlanGrp (any failure becomes E_INVALID_VALUE), records each scheme in schemesPerPortVector, returns E_INVALID_STATE for a VSPE scheme when the port has no VSPE (DPAA >= 11), and calls FmPcdKgBindPortToSchemes (error returned). The policer parameters p_PlcrParams are dereferenced only for pcdSupport PLCR_ONLY and PRS_AND_PLCR: there h_Profile must be set and valid (E_INVALID_STATE otherwise) and the profile id is written to the parse NIA or ORed into savedBmiNia. CC_ONLY (and the CAPWAP CC variants) require an offline-parsing port (E_INVALID_OPERATION). With PRS it maps firstPrsHdr to a header number (E_NOT_SUPPORTED if illegal), writes the parser NIA according to the pcdSupport combination (PRS_AND_PLCR writes nothing in that switch, a value not handled there gives E_INVALID_STATE, and E_INVALID_VALUE if a direct scheme is not among the port's schemes), configures the parser start offset, the stop/enable bits and the additional header parameters (errors E_INVALID_VALUE from AdditionalPrsParams etc.), and finally writes the initial parse result registers. It returns E_OK at the end. Partial register writes done before a later error are not undone by this function.
note: Reviewers: original right (no check of the PLCR params in the consistency test, 1222-1226); round 15 not supported by the code as stated: p_PlcrParams is only touched for PLCR_ONLY and PRS_AND_PLCR (1324-1331); it is right that other PLCR combinations are not validated here. Partly read: lines 1430-1640 (parser header configuration, soft sequence attach, error returns only) not read line by line.

name: FmSetNumOfOpenDmas
prose: Sets the number of open DMAs for one FM port (fm_ncsw.c:2808-2953; the slice cut the head). p_NumOfOpenDmas and p_NumOfExtraOpenDmas are in/out: their values are read as the request at entry (2818) and, in two paths, overwritten with the values read from the registers (2868-2869 and 2906-2907). Asserts 1 <= hardwarePortId <= 63. Guest with no mapped registers but an IPC session: it sends an FM_SET_NUM_OF_OPEN_DMAS IPC message, returns the IPC error (MINOR) if sending fails, E_INVALID_VALUE if the reply length is wrong, else the reply's error code, and does nothing else. Otherwise the behaviour depends on build options: with FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS any non-master guest returns E_NOT_SUPPORTED; without it a non-master guest with mapped registers and FM major revision >= 6 either (when the requested count is 0) reads the current counts from the registers into the two output pointers, or writes the requested counts with fman_set_num_of_open_dmas, and continues; any other non-master guest returns E_NOT_SUPPORTED (so E_NOT_SUPPORTED is returned in more than the no-IPC/no-register case). Then, if !initialConfig it reads the current per-port values; with FM_NO_GUARANTEED_RESET_VALUES and a requested count of 0 it takes the register values into the pool/accumulated counters and the output pointers and returns E_OK. Otherwise it raises extraOpenDmasPoolSize if the new extra count exceeds the current one, checks the total against the limit (E_NOT_AVAILABLE when FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS and rev < 6 exceed maxNumOfOpenDmas, or rev >= 6 exceeds DMA_THRESH_MAX_COMMQ + 1, except rev 6.0 when the A006981 errata macro is defined); if within limits it updates accumulatedNumOfOpenDmas (minus the current value, plus the request) and writes the DMA counts to the registers. Returns E_OK at the end, or the errors above.
note: Reviewers: round 15 right (E_NOT_SUPPORTED also for guests with registers when FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS or rev < 6, 2855-2881); round 17 right (the pointers are in/out, 2818, 2906-2907). Not verified: the exact argument computed in the fman_set_num_of_open_dmas calls (lines 2877, 2943 truncated in my view) and the build-time values of the FM_* macros.

name: qman_retire_fq
prose: Static t_Error (qm_portal_fqr.c:274-330) that retires a frame queue. It returns E_INVALID_STATE (via SANITY_CHECK_RETURN_ERROR) unless p_Fq->state is parked or sched, and E_INVALID_VALUE if QMAN_FQ_FLAG_NO_MODIFY is set, both before taking any lock and without touching *p_Flags. It then takes the portal lock (NCSW_PLOCK) and the FQ lock; if QMAN_FQ_STATE_CHANGING is set or the state is retired or oos it goes to out with E_BUSY, also without writing *p_Flags. Otherwise it starts a management command, fills the fqid (and, when drain is true, context_b with the FQ pointer), commits ALTER_RETIRE (or ALTER_RETIRE_CTXB when draining) and busy-waits for the result. On QM_MCR_RESULT_OK it sets QMAN_FQ_STATE_NE / ORL flags from the result's fqs bits and sets state = retired; on PENDING it sets QMAN_FQ_STATE_CHANGING; any other result prints an error and sets err = E_INVALID_STATE. After the result handling (including the failure case) it stores p_Fq->flags into *p_Flags if p_Flags is non-NULL. At out it releases the FQ lock and the portal lock and returns err (E_OK for OK and PENDING). So *p_Flags is written only on the paths that actually issued the command.
note: Reviewers: original right (E_BUSY for CHANGING and E_INVALID_STATE on MC failure); round 15 right (E_BUSY and the early returns skip *p_Flags, 284-296 vs 324-325). The ASSERT_COND at 305 has an operator-precedence quirk (compares the masked verb with the whole conditional) that I did not analyse.

name: run_rec_check_impl
prose: Static int (raidz_test.c:470-584) that tests one reconstruction function fn (index into the rec_tgts table: P, Q, R, PQ, PR, QR, PQR) over combinations of data columns and returns the number of failing combinations (err, starting at 0; it is a count, not an errno). It copies the three target indexes for fn from rec_tgts. For fn < RAIDZ_REC_PQ it loops over one data column x0 < opts->rto_dcols; for fn < RAIDZ_REC_PQR over pairs x0 < x1; otherwise over triples x0 < x1 < x2; columns at or beyond rr_cols - parity of row 0 are skipped (continue). In each iteration it first checks rto_opts.rto_should_stop and returns the current err immediately if set (so it can return before any column of that call was corrupted), then sets the data-column targets (tgtidx[2], tgtidx[1..2], or tgtidx[0..2], as x + parity) and corrupts exactly those data columns in rm (1, 2 or 3 columns depending on the branch) with corrupt_colums; the parity columns named in tgtidx are not corrupted here. Unless opts->rto_sanity is set it calls vdev_raidz_reconstruct(rm, tgtidx, 3), then compares with cmp_data and increments err when it returns non-zero. Return value: err after all combinations, or the partial err at an early stop. Side effects: modifies rm (its column data) and logs; the contents of rm after the call are the last reconstruction attempt, not restored.
note: Reviewers: original right (the return is an accumulated failure count); round 2 right (should_stop return can come before any corruption); round 15 partly right: one data column per iteration only in the fn < PQ branch, two or three in the others (raidz_test.c:501, 531, 567). Callees not read.

name: zfs_process_add
prose: Static void (zfs_mod.c:197-596; the slice cut the head) that handles a device-add event for one vdev of a pool; it has no return value and every exit is a plain return. It returns without action if the vdev has no path, if its vdev stats say VDEV_STATE_HEALTHY, or if it is offline and not faulted. It computes fullpath (the guid as a decimal string, or the path, with the partition stripped for a whole disk; returning if the strip allocation fails), then tries zpool_vdev_online (with CHECKREMOVE|UNSPARE, plus SPARE for spares): if that succeeds and the new state is HEALTHY or DEGRADED it logs and returns. Unless pool autoreplace is on AND the disk is a whole disk (or multipath whole disk) AND physpath is known, it tries ZFS_ONLINE_FORCEFAULT and returns. It builds a by-path or by-vdev raw path; if realpath fails and it is not a multipath whole disk, it FORCEFAULTs and returns (so a realpath failure on a multipath whole disk does not return here). It returns if the vdev state is not one of degraded, faulted, removed or can't-open. Then: for a multipath whole disk it calls zpool_prepare_disk (on failure frees the output and returns); else for an unlabeled disk it calls zpool_prepare_and_label_disk (on failure frees output, FORCEFAULTs and returns; on success it mallocs a pending-device record (exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if malloc fails), appends it to g_device_list and returns, to resume at the later partition event); else (labeled) it looks up and removes the matching pending device from g_device_list (if not found it FORCEFAULTs and returns) and may rewrite path for by-id paths. On the paths that continue it builds nvroot/newvd nvlists (returning if allocation or an nvlist_add fails, after freeing), waits for the partition link (zpool_label_disk_wait; on failure frees nvroot and returns), calls zpool_vdev_attach(replace) with rebuild, retries without rebuild if it fails, logs the result and frees nvroot. So it ends in attach in only some paths; the others return as listed.
note: Slice cut the head (real function at zfs_mod.c:197). Reviewers: original right (many early returns); round 15 right (realpath failure returns only when not a multipath whole disk, zfs_mod.c:385). Callee behaviour not read.

name: zfs_retire_recv
prose: Static void event handler (zfs_retire.c:366-634; the slice cut the head). It reads the vdev state from the payload and handles three groups of classes. (1) 'resource.fs.zfs.removed', or 'statechange' with state REMOVED/FAULTED: it notes whether the vdev type is spare or l2cache; returns if the vdev guid is missing or 0; for a spare it calls find_and_remove_spares and returns; returns if the pool guid is missing or find_by_guid fails; returns if the vdev is OFFLINE, and returns if the vdev is already REMOVED and the event state is REMOVED unless the class is 'removed' carrying 'by_kernel' (then skip_removal is set); unless skip_removal, for an l2arc vdev or a 'removed' class it calls zpool_vdev_remove_wanted; if it is not an l2arc and that call gave 0 and either spare_on_remove is off or replace_with_spare returns false, it logs 'no spare'; it frees devname, closes the pool and returns. (2) The resolved class returns at once; 'statechange' to HEALTHY and 'sysevent.fs.zfs.vdev_remove' call zfs_vdev_repair and return. (3) Otherwise it clears saved data, sets is_repair for the repaired class, returns if there is no suspect fault list, and for each fault: skips it if its retire flag is false; fault.fs.zfs.vdev.io sets fault_device, vdev.checksum and vdev.slow_io set degrade_device, fault.fs.zfs.device sets neither, fault.io.* is marked is_disk and then skipped (continue) without any action, other classes are skipped; for ZFS-scheme faults it needs the resource, pool guid and, unless is_repair (then vdev_guid becomes 0), the vdev guid, and a matching pool (else continue); a vdev_guid of 0 does zpool_clear on the whole pool and closes it (this also happens for a repair event with a missing vdev guid); a repair with a vdev guid clears that vdev and sets repair_done; otherwise it faults or degrades the vdev as flagged, calls replace_with_spare (its result ignored; a spare is only attempted) and closes the pool. Finally, for the repaired class with repair_done and a suspect UUID it calls fmd_case_uuresolved.
note: Reviewers: original right (fault.io.* skipped, spare replacement only attempted); round 15 right (repair events with a missing vdev guid clear the whole pool, zfs_retire.c:571-594). Helper functions not read.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the ZFS event daemon (zed.c:220-311; the slice cut the head). It initialises logging and the configuration, parses options, switches stderr logging to LOG_INFO when verbose, and calls zed_log_die (which terminates) if the effective uid is not 0 or chdir('/') fails. It closes descriptors above stderr and sets umask 0. The initial zed_conf_scan_dir(&zcp) result is checked: a negative value does exit(EXIT_FAILURE) (line 243-244); the later rescan on SIGHUP inside the main loop (line 292) ignores the result. Unless foreground it starts daemonizing and opens syslog; it installs signal handlers, optionally locks memory, writes the pid file (exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if that fails and force is not set), finishes daemonizing, logs the version, opens and reads the state file (each failure exits with EXIT_FAILURE). At the idle label it loops: zed_event_init, break if that returns false (non-zero success means retry after sleep(30) while idle mode is on and no exit was requested). If _got_exit is set at that point it jumps to out, so zed_event_fini is not called on that path. Otherwise it seeks to the saved event and runs while !_got_exit: on _got_hup it rescans the directory, and it calls zed_event_service, leaving the loop if that returns non-zero. After the loop it logs 'Exiting', calls zed_event_fini, and if do_idle is set and no exit was requested it goes back to idle; otherwise at out it destroys the conf, finalises logging and exits with EXIT_SUCCESS. It never returns from main normally; all paths end in exit or zed_log_die.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 mixed: it is right that zed_event_fini is skipped when _got_exit is set before the service loop (zed.c:283-284) and that the SIGHUP rescan at 292 ignores its result, but the initial scan at 243-244 does exit(EXIT_FAILURE) on error. Static helpers not read.

name: wait_for_children
prose: Reaps zed's child processes (zed_exec.c:200-273, void). It first sets _reap_children_stop = B_FALSE and loops while that flag stays false (the flag is set elsewhere, not in this function). Each iteration locks _launched_processes_lock and calls wait4(0, ..., wait ? 0 : WNOHANG, &usage). If wait4 returns 0 or -1 it unlocks and then: for pid 0 or errno == ECHILD it calls pause() when do_pause is set; for any other errno except EINTR it logs a warning (and does not pause); then, if do_pause is false, it returns (so with do_pause false the function returns at the first iteration where wait4 reported no child, an error, or EINTR). If wait4 returned a pid it looks it up in the launched-process tree, copies and removes the node if found (freeing the tree node), unlocks, increments _launched_processes_limit atomically, adds system time to user time in usage, logs a 'Finished' line with exit status, signal or raw status, frees node.name (a NULL name when the pid was not found) and continues the loop, also when do_pause is false. So it returns only when do_pause is false and wait4 gave no child, or when the stop flag is set during the loop; with do_pause true it does not return on ECHILD or pid 0 but pauses and loops until the flag is set.
note: Reviewers: original right (it returns on 'no child' when do_pause is false, not only on the stop flag); round 15 right (pause only on pid 0 or ECHILD, other errors just warn, zed_exec.c:212-218). The place where _reap_children_stop is set was not read.

name: share_mount_one
prose: Static int (zfs_main.c:7163-7390) that mounts or shares one filesystem and returns 0 or 1. Most checks return 0 quietly when explicit is false and print a message and return 1 when explicit is true: dataset zoned and we are in the global zone, or not zoned but in a non-global zone; op share with both sharenfs and sharesmb 'off' (legacy share); mountpoint 'legacy' or 'none'; canmount == off; encryption key unavailable (unless MS_CRYPT is in flags); an inconsistent dataset with a receive-resume token; a redacted dataset without MS_FORCE; and, for share, a filesystem already shared according to the nfs/smb combination; for mount, one already mounted without a remount option. The canmount == noauto case is special: only when !explicit, op mount returns 0 and op share on an unmounted filesystem calls zfs_unshare (result ignored) and returns 0, so a skipped noauto share does still call zfs_unshare; with explicit set, noauto passes through and does not return 1. After the checks: share (OP_SHARE) mounts the filesystem first if it is not mounted (return 1 if zfs_mount fails) and then calls zfs_share (return 1 on failure); mount (OP_MOUNT) calls zfs_mount with the given options and returns 1 on failure. Otherwise it returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (noauto share with !explicit still calls zfs_unshare, 7279-7282); round 15 right (explicit canmount=noauto passes through, 7271). Callee behaviour not read.

name: main
prose: The slice is the tail of main (zinject.c:914-1527; no function named zinject_parse_args exists). In this tail, after the option loop (lines 914-1289, not read), main picks the injection mode and validates it, with every error path calling libzfs_fini(g_zfs) before returning: raw (-b) mode returns 2 (after usage()) if combined with other options or if argc != 1, returns 1 if error == ENXIO or the -e option is used with a delay command, or if translate_raw fails; panic (-p) returns 2 for incompatible options or when argc is not 1 or 2; import/export delay returns 2 for incompatible options or when argc != 1 or zi_duration <= 0 (so an invalid duration -s <= 0 is exit status 2, not 1); ignore-writes (-I) returns 2 for incompatible options, for nowrites == 0, for both -s and -g, or for argc != 1; with no type (TYPE_INVAL) it returns 2 if flags is 0 or if there are extra arguments (unless a pool name is given with ZINJECT_UNLOAD_SPA); otherwise (data/object injection) it returns 2 if argc != 1, and returns 1 for error types ENXIO/EILSEQ, for -C combined with decrypt/decompress errors, for -e combined with delay injection, for decrypt errors on non-data types, or if translate_record fails. Next, when a dataset was selected and domount is set, it opens it and unmounts it (return 1 if zfs_open or zfs_unmount fails). It then stores the error in the record, calls ret = register_handler(pool, flags, &record, quiet); if the dataset was unmounted it then re-mounts and OVERWRITES ret with (zfs_mount(...) != 0), so a failed registration is reported as 0 when the re-mount succeeds. Finally it calls libzfs_fini and returns ret. (The re-mount happens only when dataset[0] != 0 and domount.)
note: Slice is the tail of main. Not read: the option-parsing part of main (914-1289) and register_handler/translate_*. Reviewers: round 15 right (ret is overwritten by the mount result, 1519-1522); round 17 right (invalid -s duration returns 2, line 1371-1377).

name: zpool_do_wait
prose: Implements 'zpool wait' (zpool_main.c:13472-13624; the slice cut the head). It initialises a wait_data_t (scripted, exact, headers_once, should_exit all false; mutex and condition variable initialised; every wait activity enabled) and parses options with getopt using the option string 'HpT:t:' (the 'n' case in the switch cannot be reached through that string): H scripted, p exact, T timestamp, t a comma-separated activity list (an unknown name prints 'invalid activity' and calls usage()); '?' prints 'invalid option' and calls usage(). It then calls get_interval_count; a non-zero count, a missing pool argument or more than one pool argument print a message and call usage(B_FALSE). A non-zero interval turns verbose on. It opens the pool and returns 1 if zpool_open fails (the mutex and cv created above are not destroyed on that return). In verbose mode it creates the status thread; if pthread_create fails it prints a message, closes the pool and returns 1 without destroying the mutex and condition variable (13570-13576). Then it loops: for each enabled activity it calls zpool_wait_status, stopping the inner loop on an error or a missing pool; the outer loop ends when error != 0, missing is set, or no activity was waited for. It closes the pool; in verbose mode it sets wd_should_exit under the mutex, signals the cv, joins the status thread and, if the thread's status is non-zero, replaces error with it. It then destroys the mutex and cv (only on this path) and returns error (0 on success).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (pthread_create failure and the zpool_open failure skip the mutex/cv destroy). usage() is assumed not to return (not read). Helpers not read.

name: zpool_do_online
prose: Implements 'zpool online [-e] [--power] pool device...' (zpool_main.c:7985-8102). Options: -e sets ZFS_ONLINE_EXPAND, --power (or the environment variable ZPOOL_AUTO_POWER_ON_SLOT) sets is_power_on; an invalid option prints a message and calls usage(B_FALSE). A missing pool name or missing device name prints a message and calls usage(B_FALSE). It returns 1 if zpool_open fails (after printing a message). For each device argument: if is_power_on it calls zpool_power_on_and_disk_wait and, for a non-zero rc (printing a message when ENOTSUP), returns rc immediately without calling zpool_close (so the pool handle is leaked on that path and the return value is the errno-style rc, not 0 or 1). It then looks the vdev up with zpool_find_vdev; if not found it prints a message, sets ret = 1 and continues to the next device. It reads the vdev's old state, calls zpool_vdev_online: on failure it prints the error and sets ret = 1; on success, if the new state is not HEALTHY it prints a warning with a hint (use 'zpool clear' for faulted, 'zpool replace' otherwise), and if -e was given it also prints an error or warning about expansion, with ret = 1 and a break out of the device loop only when the old state was >= VDEV_STATE_DEGRADED (degraded or healthy, i.e. not faulted). After the loop it calls zpool_close and returns ret (0 or 1).
note: Reviewers: original right (power-on failure returns rc without zpool_close); round 2 right (the >= DEGRADED test covers degraded/healthy, 8083-8085); round 15 right (return 1 when zpool_open fails, 8033-8037).

name: zstream_do_dump
prose: Implements 'zstream dump' (zstream_dump.c:209-813; the packet name main does not exist in this file, the slice cut the head). It allocates a SPA_MAXBLOCKSIZE buffer (safe_malloc) and parses options -v (twice gives very verbose), -C (no checksum check), -d (dump: sets verbose and very verbose); a missing option argument or an invalid option prints a message and calls zstream_usage(). It opens the stream from the named file (exit(1) if fopen fails) or uses stdin (exit(1) with a message when stdin is a terminal). It then reads headers in a loop (read_hdr): on the first record a byte-swapped magic selects byte-swap mode, any other bad magic prints 'Invalid stream (bad magic number)' and exit(1)s; a record type >= DRR_NUMTYPES prints 'INVALID record found' / 'Aborting.' and exit(1)s. For each valid record it counts per-type record number, adds the header size to the overhead and processes it in a per-type switch (BEGIN, END, OBJECT, FREEOBJECTS, WRITE, WRITE_BYREF, FREE, SPILL, WRITE_EMBEDDED, OBJECT_RANGE, REDACT; byte-swapping fields when needed); the printing of record contents depends on verbose (for example REDACT and OBJECT_RANGE print only when verbose), so not every record is printed; with very verbose each record other than BEGIN also prints its checksum line. It accumulates the payload sizes. After the loop it frees the buffer and, after fletcher_4_fini, prints a SUMMARY with the per-type counts and byte counts, total records, payload size, header overhead and stream length (these totals are printed regardless of verbosity), and returns 0. Only the exits listed above terminate with a non-zero status. Not read in detail: the per-type switch bodies (lines 353-739, I checked only their control flow and the verbose gating of the last cases).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 17 right (printing depends on verbose, e.g. zstream_dump.c:747 and the OBJECT_RANGE case). Partly read: the checksum verification sections inside the END and WRITE cases.

name: zstream_do_recompress
prose: Implements 'zstream recompress [-l level] type' (zstream_recompress.c:67-382; the packet name main does not exist, the slice cut the head). It parses -l (calls zstream_usage() if the level is unparsable) and requires exactly one argument (the compression type) else zstream_usage(). The type is 'off' or a name found in zio_compress_table; an unknown type or one without a compress function prints a message and exit(2)s. A terminal on stdin prints an error and exit(1)s. It then reads dmu_replay_record_t records from stdin in a loop, re-emitting each through dump_record to stdout; BEGIN resets the stream checksum, requires only one BEGIN (VERIFY), reads the payload (growing the buffer with realloc, err(1) if realloc fails); END replaces a non-zero checksum with the running stream checksum; OBJECT, SPILL, WRITE_EMBEDDED payloads are read into the buffer unchanged; FREEOBJECTS, FREE and OBJECT_RANGE have no payload; WRITE_BYREF prints 'Deduplicated streams are not supported' and exit(1)s; an unknown record type prints a message and hits assert(B_FALSE). For DRR_WRITE: an encrypted record (non-zero salt) is passed through unchanged; otherwise an invalid compression type in the stream exit(3)s, a stream type without a decompress function is treated as uncompressed, the payload is decompressed if needed (decompression failure exit(4)s) and, when the target type is not 'off', recompressed at the requested level and stored compressed only if the rounded compressed size is smaller than the logical size (else stored uncompressed with compression type and compressed size set to 0). When the target type is 'off' the decompressed data is written directly into buf (dbuf aliases buf), the record's compression type and compressed size are set to 0 and the payload is therefore the uncompressed data. EOF or error on stdout exits with status 1. After the loop it frees the buffer, shuts the subsystems down and returns 0 (also if dump_record returned non-zero, which only breaks out of the loop).
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 17 WRONG: with ctype off dbuf = buf (zstream_recompress.c:250-251), so zio_decompress_data writes the uncompressed payload straight into buf and no further copy is needed. Callee bodies (dump_record, zio_*) not read.

name: raidz_scratch_verify
prose: Static void (ztest.c:3964-4050) that checks the RAIDZ-expansion scratch state in the uberblock. It asserts raidz_expand_pause_point == RAIDZ_EXPAND_PAUSE_NONE (ASSERT) and returns at once if ztest_scratch_state->zs_raidz_scratch_verify_pause is 0 (no further effect). Otherwise it initialises the kernel in read mode (kernel_init(SPA_MODE_READ)), looks the test pool up in the namespace under spa_namespace_enter/exit, sets ZFS_IMPORT_SKIP_MMP in spa_import_flags, opens it with spa_open (VERIFY0), and asserts RRSS_GET_OFFSET(&spa->spa_uberblock) != UINT64_MAX; this assertion is made whether or not spa_raidz_expand is set. It then takes ztest_vdev_lock and the SCL_ALL config lock as reader. If spa->spa_raidz_expand is NULL it skips the state checks (goto out); otherwise it looks up the top-level vdev, reads the uberblock scratch offset and state, computes logical_size = P2ALIGN(VDEV_BOOT_SIZE, 1 << ashift) * children and asserts, by state: NOT_IN_USE offset == 0; VALID, INVALID_SYNCED and INVALID_SYNCED_ON_IMPORT offset == logical_size; INVALID_SYNCED_REFLOW offset >= logical_size. At out it releases the config lock and the vdev lock, sets zs_raidz_scratch_verify_pause = 0, closes the pool and calls kernel_fini. The checks are ASSERTs (abort on failure in builds where they are enabled), so the function has no return value.
note: Reviewers: original right (offset checks skipped when spa_raidz_expand is NULL); round 15 right (the uberblock offset != UINT64_MAX assertion at ztest.c:3987 runs before that NULL test).
